s: A global ecommerce company has many data centers worldwide. The company needs scalable cloud storage for legacy file applications. Requirements: Must support iSCSI access from on-premises servers. Must support point-in-time snapshots via AWS Backup. Must retain low-latency access to frequently accessed data. Which solution will meet these requirements?
o: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway tape gateway with S3 and AWS Backup.
Use Amazon FSx File Gateway and S3 File Gateway. Use AWS Backup.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway volume gateway in cache mode. Back up the volumes using AWS Backup.
Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway in cache mode. Use AWS Backup.
e: C is correct because the Storage Gateway Volume Gateway in cache mode supportsiSCSI block storage, which is exactly what legacy applications need. It also caches frequently accessed data locally for low-latency performance and integrates with AWS Backup for point-in-time copies. A is incorrect — tape gateway is designed for archival backup only. B and D are incorrect because FSx and file gateway offer file(NFS/SMB) storage, not block/iSCSI support. Reference: Volume Gateway Overview AWS Backup Integration

w.y: The deciding words are iSCSI access, AWS Backup snapshots, and low-latency access to frequently used data. Storage Gateway Volume Gateway is the only gateway type that presents iSCSI block volumes; cached mode keeps hot data on premises while storing the full volume in S3, and AWS Backup can take point-in-time snapshots of the volumes.

o.A: Tape Gateway presents a virtual tape library for backup software, not general iSCSI block storage for applications.
o.B: File gateways use SMB/NFS, not iSCSI, and FSx File Gateway is closed to new customers.
o.C: Correct: Volume Gateway cached mode gives iSCSI volumes with a local cache for hot data, and AWS Backup manages its snapshots.
o.D: S3 File Gateway offers NFS/SMB file shares, not iSCSI block access.
